root_cause: The datepicker does not hide on blur when the entered date is outside the allowed range, because the update/setDate logic early exits without hiding and no blur listener is registered to close the picker.
repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls this.picker.hide() to ensure the datepicker closes when the input loses focus, regardless of validation outcome.
expected_accessibility_effect: Ensures keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker calendar will close, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur may affect workflows where users expect the picker to remain open while interacting with other controls, but this aligns with typical datepicker behavior.
verification_requirements: After edit, typing a valid or invalid date and pressing Tab results in the datepicker closing (.datepicker not visible) and focus moving to the next element.
Selecting a date from the picker and then tabbing away also closes the picker.
All existing date selection and navigation functionality remains intact.
